statement: A rectangle has vertices at $(-2, 1)$, $(5, 1)$, $(5, 4)$ and $(-2, 4)$. What is the area of the rectangle?

choices.misconception: I found the width as 5 - 2 = 3, forgetting that the left side is at negative 2, so I got 3 times 3 = 9.
I added the width 7 and the height 3 instead of multiplying them.
I measured the width only from the y-axis to x = 5, so I used 5 times 3 = 15.
I found the perimeter, 2 times (7 + 3) = 20, instead of the area.

hints: Find the length of a horizontal side and of a vertical side.
A horizontal side runs from $x = -2$ to $x = 5$, so its length is $5 - (-2)$. A vertical side runs from $y = 1$ to $y = 4$.
The width is $7$ and the height is $3$. Multiply them.

solutions.reliable: The horizontal sides have length $5 - (-2) = 7$ and the vertical sides have length $4 - 1 = 3$. The area is $7 \cdot 3 = 21$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
